status: implemented; not yet submitted or trained
question: Does interleaving physical clocks across systems improve learned geometry and motion relative to synchronized clock phases?

motivation.interpretation: Clock, learning-rate phase and training age are confounded. Catastrophic forgetting is a hypothesis, not an established diagnosis.

intervention: A seed-specific balanced assignment of per-system clock phase offsets; rotate through all clocks twice per six dynamic visits, preserving H4/H8 order. Static sampling unchanged.
controls: Same base bridge architecture (no direct-time FiLM), original released static PVB warmstart, optimizer, 16384 updates, TRAIN512 protein, TRAIN1024 complex, 2569 static proteins, task ratio, four training queries, same seeds71/72. No new data or objective.
rng: Independent offset RNG does not consume task/system/record selection RNG. Different clock records are expected; sample identities and gradients need not match.
exposure: Complex has six complete dynamic visits per system; protein has twelve. Thus final per-system clock x history counts match original. Early clock coverage changes by design. No exact per-minibatch clock balance claim.
evaluation: Fixed final16384, original16 complex systems/256 forecasts and48 protein systems/192 forecasts, same native80ps and100ps protocols; protein80ps clock response as well. Compare same-seed synchronized baseline and released PVB, with system-paired intervals and full CA/pair-distance path scores. No best-checkpoint selection.
resource_plan: Seed71 uses GPU5 only after dynamic-control owner967684 exits; seed72 uses GPU1 only after owner967982 exits. Existing four bridge trainings and GPU4/7 reference/evaluation jobs unchanged.
success: Require a joint geometry/motion benefit across both seeds, not merely larger clock response, improved RMSF alone, or inherited PVB geometry. Reused development data does not establish independent competition.
